title: CaseBrief — short workflow and adoption survey

questions.label: What role, professional status and work period do your answers represent?
questions.hint: Current/former/retired; jurisdiction; personal or office-wide experience. No names needed.

questions.label: Which tools work well today, and where do you still work outside them?
questions.hint: CMS, documents, spreadsheets, research tools and any duplicate-entry burden. None/unknown is useful.

questions.label: Which one task would be most useful to improve?
options: Finding facts and original source passages
Taking over or handing off a case

questions.label: How often did that task cause difficulty in your most recent 30 working days, and roughly how much time did it take?
questions.hint: Count separate situations; include 0 or unknown. Give measured/estimated hours per week, including verification/corrections, and one observed consequence without case details.

questions.label: What record sizes and formats should a useful evaluation represent?
questions.hint: Approximate typical and unusually large document counts, pages or video hours; PDF/audio/video/text; scanned/OCR or languages. Unknown is fine.

questions.label: What evidence would you need before relying on an output?
questions.hint: For example: exact original passage/version; whether the passage supports the statement; uncertainty and contrary facts; named human approval; who did what and why. Describe unacceptable misses or false alerts.

questions.label: What device, accessibility, offline or approved-data requirements would constrain use?
questions.hint: Windows/Mac/mobile; available hardware; network restrictions; approved hosting/retention/provider rules. No credentials, client data or internal security details.

questions.label: What is the minimum integration needed to avoid another disconnected tool?
questions.hint: Approved import/export, CMS connection, source of truth, Word/PDF workflow, handoffs, migration limits; or no integration needed.

questions.label: Who would approve a fictional-data evaluation, a real-data pilot and a purchase, and how long might each take?
questions.hint: Roles/offices only; workflow owner, IT/security, procurement and budget owner. Note policy/contract blockers, training capacity and budget cycle. Unknown is valid.

questions.label: What post-pilot spending and onboarding effort could realistically be considered?
questions.hint: Your own unprompted estimate: USD amount/range, per user/month or office/year, seats, one-time costs, approval authority and basis. Zero/unknown is useful; no purchase commitment.

questions.label: What would make a short fictional-case test useful, and would you consider participating?
questions.hint: Success measures, stop conditions, available review time and a current-workflow comparison. Interest does not commit an office or authorise client data.
